name: Ecommerce
title: Ecommerce analytics, cookieless and EU-hosted
description: Cookieless, EU-hosted product analytics for online stores. Build checkout funnels, track cart abandonment, and see repeat-purchase cohorts, with no consent banner for anonymous visitors. Free for 10,000 events a month.
tagline: Checkout funnels and repeat-purchase cohorts, not just pageview counts.
intro: Most store dashboards count pageviews and sessions. Selling more comes from a different question: where do carts fall out of the checkout, and which buyers come back. Privytics is product analytics for commerce, so you map real events onto add-to-cart, checkout, and purchase, then read them as funnels and cohorts. It is cookieless and EU-hosted in Germany, so consent banners do not suppress your conversion data for anonymous visitors.

why.title: Funnels and cart-abandonment beat pageview counters
why.body: A pageview count cannot tell you where money leaks. A checkout funnel can. Line up add_to_cart, checkout_started, and purchase_completed, and the drop-off at each step shows you exactly where carts are abandoned.

why.title: Repeat-purchase cohorts show real retention
why.body: One-time revenue hides churn. Group buyers by their first purchase and watch how many come back over the following weeks. That repeat-purchase view tells you whether growth is real or just paid acquisition topping up a leaky store.

why.title: Cookieless keeps your conversion data
why.body: Consent banners suppress the very conversions you want to measure, because visitors who decline are never counted. Privytics uses an anonymous visitor id that resets every day and stores nothing on the device, so anonymous shopping needs no banner and your funnel stays complete.

why.title: Works on any platform or gateway
why.body: Privytics tracks events, not a specific checkout. Add it to Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix, or a custom stack, and send purchase events from any payment gateway. The funnels and cohorts look the same whatever runs underneath.

steps.title: Add Privytics to your store
steps.body: Drop the install snippet into your store theme so it loads on every page. On Shopify you add it to theme.liquid, on WooCommerce or any WordPress store through the theme header or a code-injection plugin, on BigCommerce through the script manager, and on Wix through custom code in the site settings. The snippet below is the generic path that works anywhere you can add HTML. Replace YOUR_CLIENT_ID with your project id from Privytics.

<script>

steps.title: Track your key commerce events
steps.body: Send an event at each moment that matters, with revenue and currency so Privytics can total sales. Call these from your theme, your cart scripts, or your order-confirmation page. Use consistent names like add_to_cart, checkout_started, and purchase_completed so they line up cleanly into a funnel later.

steps.title: Build a checkout funnel and read the cohorts
steps.body: In Privytics, create a funnel from your three events and read the drop-off at each step to find where carts are lost. Break purchase_completed down by product_id to see best sellers and total revenue, then open retention and group buyers by first purchase date to see repeat-purchase cohorts.
steps.code:
Funnel:
  1. add_to_cart
  2. checkout_started
  3. purchase_completed
  -> drop-off per step = where carts are lost

Revenue:
  break down purchase_completed by product_id
  sum the revenue property for total sales

Retention:
  group buyers by first purchase date
  -> repeat-purchase cohorts over the following weeks

faq.q: Which store platforms does Privytics work with?
faq.a: Any platform where you can add a script tag or call the REST API. That includes Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, and Wix, plus custom and headless stores. Because Privytics tracks events rather than a specific checkout, your payment gateway does not matter.

faq.q: Do I need a cookie consent banner?
faq.a: For anonymous visitors, no. Privytics is cookieless: it derives a daily-rotating salted-hash visitor id and stores nothing on the device, so there is no cookie to consent to. If you later identify logged-in customers or add other marketing cookies to your store, check your own obligations for those.

faq.q: Can I see revenue and best sellers?
faq.a: Yes. Send a revenue and currency property with your purchase event, and Privytics totals sales for you. Break purchase_completed down by product_id to rank best sellers, and by any other property you send, such as collection or campaign.
The free tier covers 10,000 events a month with no card and 12-month retention, which is plenty for a small or new store. Paid plans add session replay and 5-year event history when you need them.

faq.q: Is it accurate with ad blockers?
faq.a: Mostly, but be honest with yourself: browser events can miss a few visitors who run aggressive blockers, so client-side counts run slightly under reality. For the most complete purchase data, send purchase_completed from your server through the REST API, which no blocker can stop.

faq.q: When is another tool a better fit?
faq.a: If your main need is deep ad-spend attribution, tying every sale back to specific ad campaigns and calculating return on ad spend across networks, a dedicated attribution tool will serve you better. Privytics shows you on-site behavior, funnels, and repeat purchases, not multi-touch ad attribution.

sourcesUsed: Privytics product analytics feature set: custom events, funnels, retention, cohorts, dashboards, per-user Profiles, and REST API
Privytics cookieless model: daily-rotating salted-hash visitor id, no cookies, nothing stored on the device, so anonymous tracking needs no consent banner
Privytics plans: free 10,000 events per month with no card and 12-month retention; paid adds session replay and 5-year retention; managed, with event data stored in EU data centres in Germany
OpenPanel open-source engine that Privytics is built on: window.op track API and the browser install snippet
Store platform reference: Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, and Wix all support adding a custom script or pixel to the storefront
omitted: Event names (add_to_cart, checkout_started, purchase_completed) are conventions you define, not built-in commerce events. Privytics tracks whatever names you send, so you must fire them from your theme, cart, and order pages yourself.
Per-platform install is described in prose only, not as step-by-step guides, since this umbrella page has no docsUrl. The exact insertion point differs per platform and theme.

The no-consent-banner claim is scoped to anonymous visitors under the cookieless model. Identifying logged-in customers or adding other marketing cookies to your store can still trigger consent duties, which I flagged rather than glossed over.
Ad-blocker loss: client-side browser events can undercount slightly. I noted the server-side REST API path as the mitigation rather than claiming perfect accuracy.
Revenue and best-seller reporting depend on you sending correct revenue, currency, and product_id properties.
Not surfaced on this page: Privytics is an independent European service, operated from Spain, and there is no white-label option, so the Privytics brand shows in the product.
